working: Find your steps: describe what you need in your own words, confirm the match, answer two or three questions, and get the steps with the official source and check date on every line.
Review desk: each claim sits beside the exact passage it came from. A claim reaches users only after the reviewer approves it, and the reviewer must say whether the source is still current.

Sources: a copy of each official source is saved. Checking a source again finds the claims whose passage is no longer in the text, moves them to re-check, and marks the step as under review for users.
AI drafting: paste an official text and the AI drafts claims from it. Any claim whose quoted words are not in the text word for word is dropped before it reaches the queue.
limits: Two procedures are covered, one route each: adult name change through the central gazette, and a first-name or full-name change on Aadhaar.
The steps shown are demo data. They were approved to test the flow and have not yet been checked line by line against the sources.
Source copies are pasted in by hand. Nothing checks sources on a schedule yet.
AI matching and AI drafting need a signed-in Claude account. Other visitors get keyword matching.
AI drafting is built but has not yet been tried on a real document.
next: A second, unlike procedure: transferring a vehicle after the owner's death, which depends on a separate proof-of-succession procedure.
A real review of every claim against its source, after which the demo notice comes off.
Scheduled source checks, and reports from users on what the counter actually asked for.

items: Built the review desk, with the rule that only the owner can approve a claim.
Built the user view: plain-language intake, fixed questions, steps with sources and check dates, and an honest 'we do not cover this yet'.
Built sources: saved copies, change detection, and the re-check flow.
Built AI drafting with a word-for-word check on every quoted passage.
Made the site shareable, with a saved copy for visitors who are not signed in, and added this progress record.

Tested the original pitch against official sources. Its own example differed from the official guideline: the central route asks for one newspaper notice and a signed undertaking, not two notices and a notarised affidavit.
Defined the data model: every statement shown to a user is a claim tied to a source passage, and only a human decision can mark it verified.
Separated 'old' from 'outdated': a source can be years old and still in force, and the two are recorded differently.
Found that procedures chain: a document one office asks for is often the output of another procedure.
